meta.title: Reality is weirder than science fiction
meta.source: User script (verbatim). GPS relativity ~38 µs/day (Ashby, Living Reviews in Relativity); Venus sidereal day 243.02 d vs year 224.7 d (NASA/Astronomy.com); birds are avian dinosaurs (AMNH).

scenes.name: Hook

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Reality is weirder than science fiction—and I can prove it.

spoken: Reality is weirder than science fiction, and I can prove it.

scenes.name: Time & GPS

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Time doesn’t tick at the same speed everywhere. Gravity changes it. GPS satellites need corrections just to keep your directions accurate.

scenes.note: GPS clocks gain ~38 µs/day: gravity +45, speed −7 — corrected
spoken: Time doesn't tick at the same speed everywhere. Gravity changes it. G P S satellites need corrections just to keep your directions accurate.

scenes.name: Venus

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: On Venus, a year ends before the planet finishes spinning once.

scenes.note: Venus spins once in ~243 Earth days; its year is ~225

scenes.name: Birds are dinosaurs

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: And dinosaurs? They never completely disappeared. Birds are living dinosaurs—which means a pigeon stealing your fries is technically a dinosaur encounter.

scenes.note: Birds descend from theropod dinosaurs — living dinosaurs
spoken: And dinosaurs? They never completely disappeared. Birds are living dinosaurs, which means a pigeon stealing your fries is technically a dinosaur encounter.
